To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
natural phosphate-supported platinum catalysts can be used for the selective hydrogenation of the α,β- unsaturated carbonyl crotonaldehyde.

the use of natural phosphates as supports for platinum catalysts leads to new surface interactions, as evidenced by the XPS data, which results in high activity and selectivity for the liquid-phase selective reduction of crotonaldeyde to crotyl aldehyde.

the use of natural phosphates as support for platinum allows the preparation of systems that are active in the liquid-phase selective catalytic hydrogenation of crotoaldehyde to crolyl alcohol and the most active system is that prepared with the natural phosphate of Khouribga, which contains a high amount of iron.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the valorisation of natural phosphates as support for platinum, leading to new catalysts with high activity in the selective hydrogenation of unsaturated aldehydes.
the development of a new catalytic system, based on the use of natural phosphate as support, which is able to perform the selective hydrogenation of a challenging α,β- unsaturated carbonyl substrate.
the valorisation of natural phosphate as catalyst support, the use of XPS to determine the surface structure and the application of this system to a liquid-phase selective reaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the activity of the Pt/NaPO(4) system is due to the interaction of platinum with the support and the presence of FeCl(2), which is a strong electron-withdrawing agent that increases the Lewis acidity of the support and thus the interaction of Pt(0) with the support.
the catalytic performance is strongly dependent on the surface structure and that the latter can be modified by the addition of FeCl(2).

the most active systems are those that present the highest surface concentration of Pt and the lowest surface concentration of P, Ca, O, F and Cl, and that this is a consequence of the formation of a new surface structure, as evidenced by XPS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
natural phosphate is a good support for Pt and that it can be modified to improve the activity and selectivity of the catalysts.
the natural phosphate is a good support for platinum, which is a promising catalyst for the selective hydrogenation of α,β- unsaturated aldehydes to the corresponding unsaturation alcohols.
the use of natural phosphates as supports for Pt catalysts is a promising alternative for the selective hydrogenation of unsaturated aldehydes to the corresponding alcohols.
The main takeaway from our work is that

natural phosphates can be used as support for platinum catalysts and that the surface structure of the resulting systems is related to catalytic performance in the liquid-phase selective reduction of α,β- unsaturated aldehydes to the corresponding unsatured alcohols.
natural phosphates are a promising support for the preparation of platinum-based catalysts and can be used to produce crotyl alcohol in a selective way.
the use of natural phosphates as support for platinum allows the selective hydrogenation of α,β- unsaturated carbonyl compounds to the corresponding unsatured alcohols.
